# 3.3 Knapsack family: 0/1, unbounded, bounded

Phase 3 (Recursion to dynamic programming), target rating 1500–1900. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Each item at most once (`zero-one`)

Choose a subset of items with total weight ≤ W maximising value, W up to about 10^5.

**Works because:** Items are independent and the capacity is small enough to index the states.

### Small values, huge weights (`value-indexed`)

Weights are up to 10^9 but total value is small: dp over value storing minimum weight.

**Works because:** The total value is small enough to index the states.

### Unlimited copies (`unbounded`)

Each item may be used any number of times (coin change: number of ways or minimum coins).

**Works because:** Copies are unlimited, so the capacity loop runs upward and may reuse the current item.

### Which totals are reachable (`subset-sums`)

Decide or list which sums can be formed from the items, optionally with a bitset.

**Works because:** The range of possible sums is small.

### Limited copies (`bounded`)

Item i may be used up to c_i times; split it into power-of-two bundles and run the at-most-once version.

**Works because:** Bundles of sizes 1, 2, 4, …, plus a remainder can form every count from 0 to c_i and nothing more.
